sections.heading: The gift of song
sections.translation:
From the Muses and Apollo, who shoots from afar,
come singers and lyre players on earth;
from Zeus come kings.
Fortunate is anyone the Muses love:
sweet speech flows from his mouth.

Someone may be wasting away with a wounded heart,
his spirit weighed down by fresh grief.
But when a singer, a servant of the Muses,
sings of the glorious deeds of people long ago
and the blessed gods who live on Olympus,
he soon forgets his sadness and remembers none of his troubles.
So quickly do the goddesses’ gifts turn his thoughts away.
sections.summary: The Muses and Apollo give people music and song. A singer’s song can make someone forget their grief.

cards.label: Muses
cards.general: Goddesses who inspire poetry, song, and other arts.
cards.here: They give singers their gifts, and their songs bring relief from grief.

cards.label: Apollo
cards.general: A god associated with music and archery.
cards.here: He gives people music along with the Muses. “Who shoots from afar” refers to his skill with a bow.

cards.label: Lyre
cards.general: A stringed instrument played by plucking, often used to accompany singing.
cards.here: Lyre players receive their gifts from the Muses and Apollo.

cards.label: Zeus
cards.general: The king of the Greek gods.
cards.here: Kings owe their position and authority to him.

cards.label: Olympus
cards.general: A mountain in Greece regarded as the home of the gods.
cards.here: The singer celebrates the gods who live there.

cards.label: Blessed
cards.here: The word describes the gods’ happy existence.
